There are no streams, lakes or ponds in the area which support marine or aquatic species, except summer stocking of Holler Park pond.
Local Climatological Summary
The Milwaukee National Weather Service Office and observation station is located just northwest of the Airport Terminal Building at General Mitchell Field and would be adjacent to the east terminus of the proposed Airport Spur facility. See figure 10. All of the proposed Airport Spur corridor locations are within five miles of the Lake Michigan shoreline. The observation station is located approximately three miles west of the Lake Michigan shoreline.
According to the National Weather Services' published

Local Climatological Summary, the climate of Milwaukee (and therefore the study area) is influenced by the general storms which move eastward across the upper Ohio River valley and the Great Lakes region. Large high pressure systems moving souteastward out of Canada also have a pronounced effect on the Milwaukee climate and it is seldom that a period of more than 2 or 3 days will pass without a distinct change in the weather, particularly during the winter and spring months. Some of the most severe snowstorms which produce in excess of 10 inches develop near the Oklahoma Panhandle and pass across northern Indiana about 140 miles south of Milwaukee.
